title: Debating After School
paragraph: Every Thursday, our school has a debate club, and this week the topic is whether students should wear uniforms. I was given the side that agrees, which is not my real opinion, so I have to think carefully. I wrote three clear points: uniforms save time, they reduce pressure, and they make everyone feel equal. When the other team speaks, I will listen closely and take notes. Then I will answer one point at a time, in a calm voice. Winning is nice, but the real goal is learning to explain an idea clearly.
tongue_twisters: Clear points make a calm, confident case.
Students should speak simply and stand straight.
Listen closely, then answer calmly.

title: Sharing a Flat
paragraph: I share a flat with three other students, and we have learned that good communication solves most problems. At the start of the semester, we made a chart for cleaning, cooking, and paying bills. Sometimes someone forgets a chore, but we talk about it politely instead of getting angry. Every Sunday evening, we sit together with tea and plan the week. It is not always perfect, but I enjoy the noise, the shared meals, and the late-night conversations. Living with others has taught me to be patient and flexible.
tongue_twisters: Four friends share one fresh kitchen.
Chores and chats at the check-in table.
Polite people patiently plan the week.

title: Crossing the Desert by Jeep
paragraph: Our jeep rolled slowly across the desert, kicking up clouds of golden dust. The guide, Hamza, pointed out camel tracks and explained how the wind shapes the dunes. By noon, the heat was strong, so we stopped under a small tree and drank cold water. In the afternoon, we climbed a tall dune and watched the sun slide toward the horizon. The sand turned orange, then pink, then a soft, quiet gray. I took many photographs, but none could capture the silence of that place.
tongue_twisters: Golden dust drifts over distant dunes.
The guide goes gently through the gravel.
Camels cross the calm, quiet sand.

title: The Science Fair
paragraph: For the school science fair, my partner and I built a small model of a volcano. We mixed baking soda, vinegar, and red coloring to create the eruption. Before the judges arrived, we practiced explaining each step in simple words. When our turn came, I felt nervous, but I spoke slowly and pointed to the diagram. The judges smiled, asked a few questions, and wrote notes on their clipboards. We did not win first place, but we learned that explaining something clearly is a skill worth practicing.
tongue_twisters: Vinegar and soda start the steady eruption.
Judges jot notes on their clipboards.
Simple steps show the science.

title: A Grandfather's Watch
paragraph: My grandfather owned an old silver watch that he wore every day. It ticked loudly, and he wound it each morning with great care. When I was small, he let me hold it and listen to the ticking against my ear. After he passed away, my grandmother gave the watch to me. It no longer keeps perfect time, but I carry it in my pocket anyway. Whenever I hear it ticking, I remember his patient voice and his gentle, steady hands.
tongue_twisters: Tick, tock, the silver watch talks.
Grandfather gently wound the golden gear.
Time ticks gently through my thoughts.

title: Stuck in Traffic
paragraph: This morning, the road to my office was blocked by a long line of cars. Horns honked, motorbikes squeezed between buses, and a traffic officer waved his arms helplessly. I decided to stay calm and listen to a podcast instead of feeling angry. After forty minutes, the road finally cleared, and the cars began to move again. I arrived late, but I explained the situation politely to my manager. She smiled and said that everyone in the city understands a traffic jam.
tongue_twisters: Buses block the busy, bumpy road.
Horns honk while the traffic crawls.
Calm commuters keep cool in crowded cars.

title: The Community Garden
paragraph: On the edge of our neighborhood, there is a community garden where families grow their own vegetables. Each family has a small plot, and the paths between them are lined with colorful flowers. On Saturdays, neighbors gather to water the plants, share seeds, and exchange advice. An elderly man named Mr. Das teaches the children how to plant tomatoes. When the harvest arrives, everyone shares their vegetables at a long table. It is a simple place, but it brings people together in a surprisingly strong way.
tongue_twisters: Neighbors nurture new, neat rows of vegetables.
Fresh flowers flourish along the path.
Share seeds, share stories, share the harvest.

title: Starting a New Class
paragraph: On the first day of my evening photography class, I arrived early and chose a seat near the front. The teacher, Ms. Akter, asked each student to introduce themselves and share one reason for joining. I explained that I wanted to take better pictures of my family and travels. Others wanted to start a business or simply enjoy a new hobby. After the introductions, we learned about light, focus, and framing. I left the class tired but excited, with a notebook full of ideas and a stronger wish to keep learning.
tongue_twisters: Photographers focus on the fine, fading light.
Students share stories, then start sketching.
Frame the family photograph carefully.

title: The Fishing Village
paragraph: Early in the morning, the fishermen of the small coastal village push their wooden boats into the water. The sea is calm, and the sky is streaked with pink and gold. Women sit on the beach mending nets, chatting quietly as they work. By noon, the boats return, heavy with silver fish that glitter in the sunlight. Children run along the shore, shouting greetings to their fathers. Life here follows the rhythm of the tide, simple, steady, and deeply connected to the sea.
tongue_twisters: Wooden boats waddle through the waves.
Silver fish flash in the fisherman's net.
Steady tides shape the shoreline.

title: Thank You Speech
paragraph: At the end of the year, our class prepared a small ceremony to thank our teacher. I was chosen to give a short speech, and I wrote it carefully the night before. I wanted to mention how patient she was, how she stayed after class to help us, and how her encouragement changed our confidence. Standing in front of everyone, I took a deep breath and began slowly. By the final sentence, my voice was steady, and our teacher was smiling with tears in her eyes. It was a moment I will always remember.
tongue_twisters: Thank the teacher for her thoughtful teaching.
A steady voice shares sincere thanks.
Deep breaths bring brave, beautiful speeches.
